input.quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: Section 21.1 caps each Party at one month of Fees actually paid — far below the fallback floor of 12 months' fees and inside walk-away territory — and the words "without exception" override the Excluded Claims regime in 21.3, so indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement are all pulled inside the illusory cap. Sections 21.2 (mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages) and 21.3 (Excluded Claims definition and Customer's payment obligations not being damages) are already at the preferred position, so the shortest complete cure is to re-base the cap in 21.1 to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and delete "without exception" so the existing carve-outs operate.

proposal.summary: Raise the cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 and remove "without exception" so the Excluded Claims carve-outs operate.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, and deleted "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) genuinely sit outside the cap. A one-month fee cap that overrides all carve-outs is below our walk-away threshold.

ops.oldText: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
ops.newText: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
